checks.check: strategy and recursive Work compile through one RWO API
direct and saved-template paths produce the same graph contract
four generic concerns support two distinct agents each
dispatch admission binds the reviewed proposal into a content-addressed bundle
scripted and ARE-backed agents use one checked controller boundary
ten total runtime and capability contracts are closed and versioned
runtime and capability tests and clippy pass

observations: The first implementation incorrectly used AgentAssignment for a pre-admission need. ORCH-D21 was already precise; the code now uses AgentRequirement and reserves Assignment for the exact runtime binding.
ORCH-D3 correctly required a content-addressed complete Run Bundle. The implementation added bundle_digest and admission_context rather than weakening the definition.

ORCH-D14 through ORCH-D18 caused policies, evidence expectations, result reduction, adapter compatibility, inputs, constraints, and full proposal identity to become explicit fields. No wording change is needed at this stage.
ORCH-D46 correctly separates a button-ready Run Template preset from its immutable Strategy Template. The implementation added that missing layer rather than collapsing the two definitions.

known_limits: ARE is represented by a transport trait and tested fake; a live Gateway transport remains M6.
Strategy policies and evidence expectations are preserved and digest-bound but are not yet interpreted by a policy engine.
Template storage, catalog APIs, user-facing Run Templates, and publication governance remain M6 or later.
The Rust structs and schemas are aligned by tests, but full JSON Schema instance validation is not yet wired into an API boundary.
claim_ceiling: M5 local implementation evidence only; no live provider execution, definition promotion, result acceptance, legacy deletion, release, deployment, publication, or authority effect.
